part_B_multiple_access_surrogate.question: is the F2 'equal time-share' surrogate the right per-user uplink service test for NR, whose uplink is OFDMA?
part_B_multiple_access_surrogate.reasoning: F2 gives each of the K users 1/K of the TIME on the whole carrier: per-user UL rate = (1/K) max_n r(n). In NR uplink OFDMA a user can hold about N_PRB/K PRBs CONTINUOUSLY and concentrate its full 23 dBm on them: per-user rate = max_{n <= N_PRB/K} r(n). For a power-limited UE this is up to K times larger. For the downlink with uniform PSD the two are identical
part_B_multiple_access_surrogate.users_source: ITU-R M.2412-0 Table 5(b) Dense Urban-eMBB, 10 UEs per TRxP

F3_ofdma_share.DL: identical to F2: SE >= 2.25 bit/s/Hz (per-user 0.225 under either access scheme)
F3_ofdma_share.UL: max over n <= floor(N_PRB / 10) of n * PRB_bw * SE_UL(SNR(n)), divided by the occupied bandwidth of the WHOLE carrier, >= 0.15 bit/s/Hz (the M.2410 per-user 5th-percentile UL value itself, since the share is continuous)

part_B_multiple_access_surrogate.proved_before_run: if the uncapped F2 maximiser n* satisfies n* <= 10 n_max, then n' = ceil(n*/10) <= n_max has SNR(n') >= SNR(n*) and n' >= n*/10, hence r(n') >= r(n*)/10: F2-feasible implies F3-feasible. The only possible F2-yes/F3-no outcomes have n* > 10 n_max (PRB granularity of floor(N_PRB/10))
part_B_multiple_access_surrogate.role: analytic prediction only; E1.5.4 (10-UE 5G-LENA sector with TDMA and OFDMA schedulers) decides which surrogate describes NR

checks.S1_v16_reproduction: the V16.1.0 evaluation in this script reproduces the committed E1.4 summary.json exactly (every feasible and class fraction, every case, state, profile and mix; float equality)
checks.S2_v19_scope: V19.5.0 changes nothing in states outdoor, in_car, indoor_low, indoor_low_indep (float equality of every fraction, every case and profile)
checks.S3_v19_e14_checks: all E1.4 checks N1-N10 pass on the V19.5.0 run (N5 and N6 evaluated with the V19.5.0 coefficients)
checks.S4_f3_allocation: every capped UL record: best n <= n_max and capped rate <= uncapped rate (+1e-9 bit/s)
checks.S5_f3_dominance: every record that is UL-feasible under F2 but not under F3 has an uncapped maximiser n* > 10 n_max (zero violations of the proved bound)
checks.S6_f3_partition: under F3, K1, K2, K3, K4, K6 partition every outcome of every case, state and version, and K6 = 0 in the shared-variate states (implied: 3.5 GHz is at least as good as 7.2 GHz for every direction in those states, including case C, by the same scaling argument as F2)

expectations_stated_before_run: A: only high-loss indoor outcomes change; the 7.2 - 3.5 GHz wall-loss difference grows from 4.61 to 4.93 dB, so K2 and K4 in high-loss buildings grow slightly; the M.2412 mix (16% high-loss) moves by well under 1 point
B: F3 uplink feasibility is much higher than F2 for power-limited (distant, indoor) links; K3 shrinks and K1 grows in every regime; the downlink is unaffected
